reason: Priests are depicted favorably through explicit selection and elevated access. Aaron (the high priest) is specifically called to ascend to the Lord alongside Moses, Nadab and Abihu (priestly sons) are chosen to come near, and seventy elders are selected to approach Mount Sinai—privileges explicitly denied to the general population. This hierarchical inclusion represents an honored and favored status. However, the passage also emphasizes strict requirements: priests must sanctify themselves, and there is a warning that God will 'break out' against them if they transgress. This admixture of privilege with solemn responsibility tempers the depiction—priests are elevated but not without qualification.
